# trashwheels

**trashwheels** helps Healthy Harbor volunteers and community educators
answer one question:

> Which kinds of rubbish does each of Baltimore's Trash Wheels collect most,
> and is it going up or down over time?

It contains cleaned data on every dumpster load the Trash Wheels collected
from 2014 to 2023, two functions to summarise and plot it, and a Shiny app
for exploring it.

**Documentation website:**
<https://etc5523-2026.github.io/etc5523-assignment-4-prat0012-ai/>

## What is in the package

| Part | What it does |
|---|---|
| `trash_loads` | The data: estimated counts of seven kinds of rubbish in each of 993 dumpster loads from the four Trash Wheels. |
| `summarise_rubbish()` | Summarises one kind of rubbish by Trash Wheel and year, including the average per dumpster load. |
| `plot_rubbish()` | Draws one line per Trash Wheel from that summary. |
| `run_app()` | Opens the Trash Wheel rubbish explorer app. |

## The data

The data come from [Mr. Trash Wheel](https://www.mrtrashwheel.com/), part
of Baltimore's Healthy Harbor initiative, and were shared through
[TidyTuesday](https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/tree/main/data/2024/2024-03-05)
on 5 March 2024. They cover 993 dumpster loads from four Trash Wheels
(Mister, Professor, Captain and Gwynnda) between May 2014 and December 2023.
Each row of `trash_loads` is one kind of rubbish in one dumpster load.

The script `data-raw/trash_loads.R` downloads the raw file and prepares it.
It fixes dates written in two formats, takes the year from the date where
the raw year column was wrong, and keeps blank counts as blank, because a
blank means the item was not counted, not that none were found.

Counts are estimates made from samples of each dumpster.

## Installation

Install the package from GitHub:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("ETC5523-2026/etc5523-assignment-4-prat0012-ai")
```

## Launch the app

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(trashwheels)
run_app()
```

The app opens in your web browser. Choose a kind of rubbish, the Trash
Wheels to compare, a range of years, and whether to show the average per
dumpster load or the yearly total. The headline, chart and table update
together, and a "Read with care" box flags weak evidence, such as years
where few loads were counted.

## A quick example

```{r example, fig.alt = "Line chart of average plastic bottles per dumpster load from 2019 to 2023 for the four Trash Wheels. Professor Trash Wheel is highest but falling."}
library(trashwheels)

bottles <- summarise_rubbish(
  trash_loads,
  item = "Plastic bottles",
  years = c(2019, 2023)
)

plot_rubbish(bottles, measure = "per_load")
```

Professor Trash Wheel collects the most plastic bottles in each dumpster
load, but its average fell from about 5,750 in 2019 to about 3,800 in 2023.
